newsitem.title: ITALY: Chairman of Italian soccer club Vicenza arrested.
newsitem.headline: Chairman of Italian soccer club Vicenza arrested.

text.p: Police on Monday said they had arrested the chairman of Italian first division soccer club Vicenza, Gianni Sacchetto, and his predecessor in the post on suspicion of bankruptcy fraud.
A finance police statement said Sacchetto and Pieraldo Dalle Carbonare, whose family owned the club until September last year, were among six people arrested in the case on Sunday.
Four people, including Sacchetto, Dalle Carbonare and his brother Sebastiano, were being held in preventive detention in Milan's San Vittore jail. Two others were under house arrest.

The arrests followed three months of investigations by Milan magistrate Alfredo Robledo linked to the collapse in June 1995 of Trevitex, a financial holding company controlled by the Dalle Carbonare family.

The police statement said all six men were suspected of conspiring fraudulently to disperse the assets of Trevitex through front companies including one called Otto Srl, which Sacchetto used to buy a 99.9 percent stake in the Vicenza club.

The statement said investigators believed Otto was owned by the Dalle Carbonare family "which pretended to cede control of Vicenza to prevent the club being included in assets subject to receivership procedures".
Judicial sources said investigators suspected that as much as $5.2 million owed to creditors of Trevitex may have found its way into Vicenza club funds.
None of the suspects had any immediate comment on the case.
Vicenza, promoted to Italy's first division at the end of the 1995 season, was put under the control of an official receiver in January as part of the investigations.
The north-eastern club faces Napoli in the final of the Italian soccer cup next month and lies eighth in the first division, giving it two chances of playing in European club competition next season.
Coach Francesco Guidolin said the club had been saddened by the arrests and expressed support for those involved.

"This is a very sad story for all those involved, our friends to whom we're closely linked... We'll have to stand by them and do the rest on the field, trying to be even better than before," Guidolin said.
Club spokesman Paolo Bedin said that the arrests would have no effect on the day-to-day running of the club.
"Neither our preparation for the (Italian) Cup final nor for the rest of the league season will be effected," Bedin said.
He acknowledged, however, that the club would face problems in its summer transfer market activity and in preparations for next season if the issue of its ownership was not resolved soon.

Bedin confirmed that a group of six Vicenza-based industrialists had made an offer to the official receiver for the club. Media reports say the offer is worth $8.8 million but that the receiver may take up to a month before deciding on it.
Neither the Italian soccer federation nor the league had any substantive comment on the case.
